Tidy Towns, Estates, and Schools applauded at the Sustainable Development Awards Ceremony 
  
Wicklow County Council held its annual Sustainable Development Awards, Tidy Main Streets & Tidy Estates Awards 
ceremony, on Saturday, 7th March in The Brockagh Centre, Laragh. Tidy Towns groups, Residents' Associations, 
schools, local & farming champions, and businesses were recognised and thanked for their pro-active role in the 
restoration of our biodiverse environment and building more sustainable and resilient communities in Co Wicklow. The 
quality of the work completed and the exceptional levels of volunteering were evident, with 72 awards handed out to 
schools, groups, businesses and individuals throughout Wicklow.  
Wicklow’s Sustainable Development Awards focuses on various themes such as Biodiversity, Climate Action, Waste 
Reduction, Built Heritage, Water Protection and Energy. In addition, three categories specifically recognised the 
outstanding work undertaken by Wicklow’s primary and secondary schools.  
The award for Biodiversity, Wildlife & Natural Amenities went to ReWild Wicklow for their deep understanding and 
appreciation of Biodiversity demonstrated through their restoration work on upland woodland areas using native trees 
grown from local seed. Roundwood Tidy Towns won the Built Environment category for their commemorative events at 
Derralossary Graveyard, while the Five Loaves Bookshop in Bray, nominated by Bray Tidy Towns, received the 
Business Award. 
Greystones Tidy Towns won the Climate Action Award for their ongoing excellent work in this category, includes 
initiatives like ‘solar meitheals’ and tree planting. A new participant, Jack’s Mill Forest Garden, was awarded the 
Communal Gardening Award for their well-planned community garden. Thanks to the Community Climate Action Fund, 
there were excellent entries in the Energy Award category, with the prize awarded to Donard Community Enterprises for 
their thoughtful energy upgrade to their community hall, which provided numerous benefits to the locality.  
Bray Golf Club won the Sustainable Tourism Award having been nominated by Bray Tidy Towns for their efforts to 
protect and enhance biodiversity on their grounds. Meanwhile, Hollywood Tidy Towns secured the Trees Award with 
their ongoing, well-planned tree planting schemes. Staying westside, Blessington Tidy Towns continues their 
outstanding projects and initiatives and secured the Waste Minimization Award. Glenwood Residents Association (Swan 
River Group) won the Water Protection Award for their work restoring river habitat and improving and enhancing this 
Bray tributary in a sensitive manner.

The Homeless HAP Place finder provides assistance in: 
• 
seeking out potential properties suitable for households currently identified as homeless or at risk of 
homelessness. 
• 
liaising with specific households to establish their specific needs. 
• 
establishing relationships with local property agents and landlords; and, 
• 
supporting those homeless households to (a) prevent the necessity to enter emergency accommodation or (b) to 
exit emergency accommodation and secure a tenancy. 
• 
To date, 690 households (483 families & 207 singles) have been assisted under the Homeless HAP Scheme in 
Wicklow County Council from the inception on 1st October 2018 to 28th February 2026. (267 homeless cases, 
376 prevention cases to date and 48 direct provision).  175 properties were sourced by WCC. 
 
Addressing Homelessness in Partnership with Approved Housing Bodies 
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – Kilmantin Hill, Wicklow 
Kilmantin Hill has 11 rooms to support persons either homeless, exiting a higher support facility, or in danger of becoming 
homeless.  
There are 9 clients supported in the Kilmantin Hill facility, operated by Dublin Simon. There is continuous transition by the 
clients to suitable alternative accommodation. 
A report is being undertaken at present to cost the refurbishment of the current rooms with a view to making them all 
ensuite. More details will be available over the coming months. 
Homeless Family Service – Fitzwilliam Road, Wicklow   
Dublin Simon are engaged by Wicklow County Council to operate and manage the facility at Fitzwilliam Road, Wicklow 
as a Family Homeless Service. The building comprises of three 1-bed units, two 2-bed units, and two 3-bed units. Eleven 
families have now transitioned or are in the process of transitioning to a permanent home and the resulting vacancies are 
in the process of being occupied with families experiencing or in danger of homelessness. 
It is envisaged that families will avail of the service for circa 6-months STA (Supported Temporary Accommodation) with 
key working support to enable families to transition from homelessness into Homeless HAP, or alternative longer-term 
accommodation.   
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – San Remo, Bray 
San Remo is operated by Dublin Simon and incorporates a service model whereby there are a number of emergency/cold 
weather initiative beds and Supported Temporary Accommodation Beds (STA). There is on site key working support 
linking in with clients.    
The Neighbourhood Liaison Committee is now operational and meets monthly. 
Bi-monthly meetings are held with Dublin Simon and Wicklow County Council staff. 
Homeless Supported Accommodation - Carraig Eden, Greystones 
This facility provides 35 ensuite bedrooms with associated kitchens and common areas and is fully operational. Wicklow 
County Council run an in-reach service with the clients to support them as they continue their journey into more permanent 
accommodation.  
Other Homeless Supported Accommodation 
Wicklow County Council owned properties in Wicklow, Bray, and Greystones, leased to Approved Housing Bodies, 
provide 12 units of low to medium supported accommodation targeted to the particular support needs of the clients. Six 
of these persons living in shared accommodation have now successfully moved into their forever homes and this in turn 
created space to move further people out of homelessness.  
A homeless outreach service has been rolled out in Bray and is proving very successful.

Housing First 
Peter McVerry Trust has been appointed as the Housing First Programme Implementer for the Mid-East Region. Wicklow 
County Council is committed to working with them and has now reached and surpassed the targets identified in the 
programme. Housing First recognises that a stable home provides the basis for recovery in other areas.  
 
Properties will be provided by both Wicklow County Council and Peter McVerry Trust for the implementation of the 
programme. 
Wicklow County Council has, to date, successfully accommodated 18 clients under Housing First.  Other clients proposed 
for Housing First have been assessed by the team and are availing of key support work pending finalisation of sourcing 
of accommodation. The main issue facing this programme is the availability of 1-bed units in suitable locations with easy 
access to required services.

Sláintecare Healthy Communities  
1. Children’s Wellness Hub 
Work on the evaluation of the Children’s Wellness Hub is progressing well. The final draft of the evaluation report from 
Mary Immaculate College is expected by the end of March. Once received, this will provide a valuable overview of the 
impact of the Hub and will help inform future development of services and programmes within the Bray Sláintecare Healthy 
Communities area. Additional supporting information and programme updates will also be included as part of this process. 
2. Bray Traveller Project 
The Bray Traveller project continues to progress positively and is currently meeting all of its key performance indicators. 
As part of the next phase of the programme, two groups of participants 6 male and 4 female, will be commencing higher 
education opportunities. This represents an important step in supporting educational progression and capacity building 
within the Traveller community and reflects the strong engagement and commitment of participants involved in the 
programme. 
3. Period Poverty Initiative 
An Expression of Interest has been submitted to the Department of Health to secure ongoing funding for the Sláintecare 
Healthy Communities Period Poverty initiative. This funding will support the continued delivery and expansion of the 
project by providing free menstrual products through community organisations and services working with vulnerable 
individuals and families. This approach aims to ensure sustained access to essential health supports. The funding will 
also enable the delivery of targeted menstrual health education workshops within disadvantaged communities, supporting 
awareness, dignity, and long-term wellbeing outcomes. 
4. Food Poverty Research Project 
This year, as part of the Sláintecare Healthy Communities programme, a community food and nutrition research project 
will be undertaken in the Bray area. The purpose of the project is to build community-informed evidence that can inform 
the future development of local interventions, planning, and policy responses. 
The research will involve a community survey followed by focus groups exploring several key areas including how 
residents interact with their local food environment, such as access, affordability, and availability of food. It will also 
examine the prevalence of food poverty and food insecurity within the context of the current cost-of-living pressures, as 
well as broader nutrition and eating habits within the community. 
To support the research process, a Research Steering Group is being established. The group will help ensure that the 
research is conducted in a high-quality, ethical, inclusive, and community-informed manner, while also supporting the 
relevance and impact of the findings. The group will meet approximately three times over the course of the project, which 
will run from March 2026 to March 2027. 
The first meeting of the Research Steering Group will take in March.

Croí Cónaithe (Towns, Cities and Rural) – Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant 
The Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant is a payment you can get if you are turning a vacant house or building into 
your permanent home or a rental property.  The grant applies to qualifying vacant properties in cities, towns, villages and 
rural parts of the country. 
There are 2 types of Grants available: 
• 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant of up to €50,000 
• 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant including the Derelict Property top up grant of up €70,000 
To qualify for the top up of €20,000, an independent report prepared by a Structural Engineer, along with a copy of their 
Professional Indemnity Insurance, is required to be submitted along with the application, confirming, to the satisfaction of 
the local authority, that the property is derelict i.e. structurally unsound and dangerous. 
 
To qualify for the grant, applicants must: 
Have proof of ownership or evidence of active negotiations to buy the property (that is, confirmation of engagement from 
the estate agent or owner of the property) where you are seeking approval in principle for a grant. 
- 
Live in the property as your principal private residence or make it available for rent. 
- 
Have proof that the property has been vacant for at least 2 years and that it was built up to and including 2007.

Wicklow CIF 
After hosting an End of Year Review of the Wicklow CIF in 2025, a new structure was agreed by all members for 2026 
to improve our ways of working together. The adoption of this new structure was to ensure effective collaboration across 
the entire county. During the End of Year Review, it was highlighted that the needs of West Wicklow and East Wicklow 
differ significantly, due to location and availability of services. Thus, resulting in the formation of the regional groups, 
West and East Wicklow. The new structure aims to address demographic needs of each region and presenting their 
work to the CIF Management group quarterly.  
The initial task of the regional groups was to discuss Good Practices that are already happening in Wicklow and 
identify their Shared Memberships. They then continued to examine the Gaps and Challenges both in their control 
and out of their control. The goal of this work is to develop a workplan designed around agreed thematic areas such as, 
Children / Young People, Education / Employment, English Language, Therapeutic / Mental Health, Family Support, 
Diversity and Inclusion, Legal Welfare / Human Rights, Health / Wellbeing and the IRPP.

Information Systems 
 
Operations  
 
• 
The IT Helpdesk continues to streamline the workflow for the technical support team with an average of 50 tickets

GIS & Systems Analysis 
• 
MyPlan Data Preparation 
Work has continued on preparing zoning datasets for submission to the MyPlan system managed by the 
Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage. This has included refining spatial data to ensure 
consistency and accuracy ahead of formal review. Supporting mapping updates have also commenced for the 
Blessington and Greystones-Delgany & Kilcoole Local Area Plans. These activities will help ensure alignment 
between local planning data and national systems. 
 
• 
Forward Planning and Data Updates 
Updates have been implemented to zoning and settlement boundaries in line with the recently adopted 
Greystones-Delgany & Kilcoole Local Planning Framework 2026. In addition, key County Development Plan 
mapping layers, including landscape categories and coastal cells, have been refreshed. Revised datasets have 
been published to internal systems and the Open Data portal. This ensures that staff and stakeholders have 
access to up-to-date and consistent planning information. 
 
• 
Call for Sites Portal Development 
Progress has been made on the development of a GIS-based Call for Sites assessment portal. Engagement 
has taken place with the Forward Planning team to define requirements and agree a structured approach. The 
portal is intended to support the submission, spatial analysis, and reporting of site proposals in a streamlined 
manner. This initiative will improve efficiency and transparency in managing future land-use submissions. 
 
• 
Broadband Mapping and Analysis 
Analysis of Fibre-to-the-Home (FttH) data has been undertaken to support broadband infrastructure insights. 
This included validation of address data and spatial review of connectivity coverage. A heatmap has been 
developed to highlight areas where premises are not yet connected. The outputs will assist in identifying gaps 
and informing future infrastructure planning. 
 
• 
Hydrant Mapping Initiative 
Work has progressed on the development of a hydrant mapping dataset in collaboration with internal 
stakeholders. Existing utility data has been extracted and prepared for use in mobile applications. The data has 
been uploaded to Field Maps for initial testing and review. This project aims to support improved access to 
infrastructure information in the field. 
 
• 
Mapping and Project Support
